result.topic_en: Page 16 of Riemann's Latin Paris prize essay on heat conduction: interpreting expression (III) as the curvature measure of a surface, the case n=3 giving six conditions on the functions b (only three independent), and a note that lack of time prevented carrying out the calculations, so only the methods and individual solutions are listed, beginning with the simplest case of the heat equation (I).

elementis initialibus variationes s sunt ut
$\alpha ds_1+\beta\delta s_1 : \alpha ds_2+\beta\delta s_2 : \cdots : \alpha ds_n+\beta\delta s_n$ deno-

unde in hoc casu sex obtinemus aequationes,
quibus functiones b satisfacere debent, ut
$\Sigma b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam constantibus coefficien-

difficile, ope notionum modo traditarum,
est demonstratu, has sex conditiones, ut hoc
fieri possit, sufficere. Observandum tamen
est ternas tantum esse a se independentes.

calculos perscribere. Contenti igitur esse
debemus, postquam methodos quibus usi
sumus exposuimus, solutiones singulas
quaestionis propositae enumerasse.

methods.what: Geodesic surface spanned by directions αds+βδs; expression (III) is its Gaussian curvature measure

methods.what: For n=3, expression II is a quadratic form in the bivector components, yielding six conditions for reducibility of the metric to constant coefficients (flatness)

items.english: Nor is it difficult, by means of the notions just presented, to demonstrate that these six conditions suffice for this to be possible.

items.english: It must be observed, however, that only three of them are independent of one another.

items.english: Now, to solve the question proposed by the most illustrious Academy, the forms of the functions b found by the method explained above must be substituted into these six equations, whereby all cases will be found in which the temperature u in homogeneous bodies can be a function of time and of only two variables.

sumus exposuimus, solutiones singulas

items.english: But shortness of time did not permit writing out these calculations. We must therefore be content, having explained the methods we used, to have enumerated the individual solutions of the proposed question.
